newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Ferrell FX Index off 0.2 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Ferrell FX Index off 0.2 pct in March.

text.p: The Ferrell FX Index fell 0.2 percent in March but rose 6.5 percent overall for the first quarter, Ferrell Capital Management said Thursday.
The median return for March was a 0.2 percent loss, with 14 of 35 programs reporting positive results.
Quantitative Financial Strategies Inc (QFS) of Conshohocken, Pa., recorded the top performance for the month, an 8.7-percent gain.
Naava Grossman, president of QFS, said long-term fundamental analysis led QFS to anticipate the March depreciation in yen and the Canadian dollar.
John W Henry & Co of Westport, Conn., turned in the second-best March performance, and Analytic TSA of Los Angeles placed third, Ferrell said.
The Ferrell FX Index is a benchmark for multi-advisor currency portfolios and includes 36 programs managed by 31 firms in the United States, UK, France, Canada, Ireland and Switzerland.
Since January 1987, the index has posted a compounded annual return of 17.9 percent.
